title: Message::sender_id field set to sender_user_id, but 'self' is used for outbound - client cannot distinguish direction
description: In insert_outbound_message(), sender_user_id is hardcoded as 'self' in the SQL. row_to_message() then sets Message.sender_id = sender_user_id. So outbound messages always have sender_id='self'. This is documented in Message's field doc ('Contact id of sender, or self for outgoing messages'). However, 'self' is a reserved Rust identifier — any future code that tries to compare sender_id with a contact id needs to handle this sentinel explicitly. More importantly, if peer_user_id happens to be the literal string 'self' (possible on a misconfigured Headscale deployment with no OIDC), a received message from such a peer would be indistinguishable from an owner-sent message. The correct fix is to use the actual owner user_id (from the self table) rather than the literal string 'self'. This would also remove the need for the sentinel-based direction check.
